To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

simultaneous enhancements in the thermoelectric performance of HH/FH nanomaterials can be achieved through the interplay between the carrier concentration and the mobility, which is a result of the unique electronic structure of the HH phase.
large increases in thermopower (S) and electrical conductivity (σ) of bulk nanostructured HH alloys are achieved simultaneously through the insertion of nanometer-scale FH inclusions in the matrix.
large enhancements in power factors and ZT of bulk half-Heuslers can be achieved through coherent insertion of nanostructured full-Heuslers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of nanostructured thermoelectric materials that exhibit simultaneous enhancements in the thermoelectric power factor and reductions in the thermal conduction.
the design of new thermoelectric materials with large thermopower and high electrical conductivity.
a new class of thermoelectric materials that are based on the HH/FH phase combination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HH/FH interface plays a crucial role in the charge transport in the nanocomposite and is responsible for the observed enhancements in the thermoelectric figure of merit.
we have demonstrated the first simultaneous large enhancements in the electrical conductivity and thermopower of bulk nanostructured materials.
the simultaneous enhancements in the power factor and reduction in the thermal conductivity through coherent insertion of FH inclusions into the HH matrix results in large enhancements in ZT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the simultaneous large enhancements in both the power factor and thermal conductivity of bulk thermoelectrics can be achieved by combining the effects of coherent nanoinclusions and nanostructuring.

the simultaneous large enhancements in the power factor and reduction in the thermal conductivity in bulk nanostructured thermoelectrics can be achieved through a judicious design and engineering of interfaces.
nanostructures can be utilized to enhance the thermoelectric properties of materials in a way that was not previously thought possible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
large improvements in thermoelectric efficiency of bulk materials can be achieved by combining nanostructuring with appropriate chemical doping.
the simultaneous enhancements in the thermoelectric properties can be achieved through nanostructuring of HH phases, which can lead to the development of new thermoelectric materials.
the thermoelectric figure of merit can be significantly enhanced by simultaneously improving the power factor and reducing the thermal conductivity through nanocomposite engineering.
